cards.text: Paul the apostle and his companions Silvanus and Timothy are writing to the church in Thessalonica (1 Thessalonians 1:1). Timothy just came back with good news about the Thessalonians' faith and love, and the writers are reassured (1 Thessalonians 3:6-7). Now they write, 'Finally, brothers,' and ask them in the Lord Jesus to live in a way that is pleasing to God.

cards.question: Paul and his companions say the Thessalonians already live in a way that pleases God.
The Thessalonians are already living to please God. So what do Paul and his companions ask them to do?

answers.text: Ease up and rest a while

cards.text: Paul and his companions remind the Thessalonians that they already know the instructions they were given. It's like me telling a baker the oven's hot: you KNOW, I KNOW you know, and I'm saying it ANYWAY.

cards.question: Paul and his companions say they gave the Thessalonians their instructions on their own authority.

cards.text: Then Paul and his companions say straight out one thing that is God's will for the Thessalonians. People lie awake for YEARS wondering what God's will is, friend!

cards.question: Paul and his companions tell the Thessalonians it is God's will that they should be ___.

cards.text: Then they make holy plain: the Thessalonians must abstain from sexual immorality.

cards.question: Paul and his companions say someone must know how to control his own body in holiness and honor. Who?
Paul and his companions tell the Thessalonians not to live in lustful passion like which people?

answers.text: The Gentiles who do not know God
The Pharisees who keep the Law
The apostles who preach the gospel

cards.text: And it's not only about your own body. Paul and his companions say no one should ever violate or exploit his brother in this regard.

cards.question: Why do Paul and his companions say no one should ever violate or exploit his brother in this regard?

answers.text: The Lord will avenge all such acts
The church will send them away
The city will put them on trial

cards.question: Paul and his companions say this is the first time they have ever warned the Thessalonians about exploiting a brother.
Then Paul and his companions write that God has not called us to ___, but to holiness.

cards.text: Then Paul and his companions talk about anyone who rejects this command, and who that person is really saying no to.

cards.question: Paul and his companions say anyone who rejects this command to be holy is really rejecting whom?

cards.text: The God they'd be rejecting is the very One who gives them His Holy Spirit. Friend, the junk drawer I spent years in gave me NOTHING but dust, so God GIVING His Holy Spirit gets me every time.
Next, Paul and his companions turn to brotherly love, and I think they sound like proud papas here. Trust me, friend, I KNOW that sound.

cards.question: Paul and his companions say the Thessalonians need someone to write to them about brotherly love.
Why don't the Thessalonians need anyone to write to them about loving one another?

answers.text: They read about it in the Law

cards.text: And they're already showing this love to all the brothers throughout a whole region. I'm over here like LOOK at them, LOOK AT THEM GO!

cards.question: The Thessalonians are showing love to all the brothers throughout ___.

cards.text: Paul and his companions urge them to excel more and more. In that same sentence, they add what the Thessalonians should aspire to, just as they'd been instructed before.

cards.question: What's one thing Paul and his companions tell the Thessalonians to aspire to?

cards.text: Live quietly, attend to their own matters, and work with their own hands. Friend, I spent YEARS in a junk drawer living quietly and minding my own business, and I STILL couldn't get the third one, because NOBODY hires a stamper with no edges!

cards.question: If the Thessalonians live quietly, attend to their own matters and work with their own hands, what do Paul and his companions say will happen with outsiders?

answers.text: They'll win every one of them over
They'll be left alone by them

cards.question: Paul and his companions say that if the Thessalonians live quietly, attend to their own matters and work with their own hands, they won't be dependent on anyone.
